step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): If you do get a blister, cover and protect the area from further irritation (p. 13).
Step 2 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): A sprain occurs when an ankle, wrist, or other joint is bent farenough to overstretch the ligaments, the tough bands that holdjoints together (p. 13).
Step 3 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): A strain occurs when muscles are overstretched, creating tears in the muscle fibers (p. 13).
Step 4 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Minor sprains and strainscause only mild discomfort, but more serious sprains and strainsmight be temporarily disabling (p. 13).

Step 3 (Alone in A Rowboat Push): Even when fully awash, the gunwale of most boats will be a few inches above the level of the water (p. 65).
Step 4 (Alone in A Rowboat Push): If you are alone and your boatswamps and yougo over the side, the best way toget back in is over the transom (p. 65).

pamphlet_excerpts: Rowing Core Field Standard: Step in with your hands on the gunwales, keep your weight low and centered, then quickly turn and sit on the midship seat (p. 67).
Rowing Core Field Standard Principle 2: Remember to keep sight of the person who needs help andto push the bow of the boat in the direction you want (p. 67).
Rowing Core Field Standard Principle 3: Use this forward momentum to your advantage while you getin position and prepare to row (p. 67).
Rowing Core Field Standard Principle 4: As soon as you are seated, slipon the life jacket and put the oars in the out position (p. 67).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Rowing Core Field Standard): Lookover your shoulder to fix your direction toward the person in the water and begin rowing (p. 67).
Step 2 (Rowing Core Field Standard): Always make your approach to a swimmer into thewind or against the current (p. 67).
Step 3 (Rowing Core Field Standard): Remember also that wavesor rough water can make launching from shoredangerous (p. 67).
Step 4 (Rowing Core Field Standard): Usually, a comparatively mild interval willfollow a series of heavy waves (p. 67).
